Analytic solutions for censored delay distributions

Source: vignettes/analytic-solutions.Rmd
analytic-solutions.Rmd

1 Introduction

For a non-uniform primary event window each analytic solution for a continuous delay in the package writes the primary event censored distribution function as a weighted sum of truncated exponential-moment transforms of the delay density[1]. The uniform window is the limit of this sum as the tilt goes to zero, and needs only the delay CDF and its partial moment. Where no tractable form applies the package integrates numerically. In R it uses pcens_cdf.default() and in Stan an ODE solver, or for some pairs a numerical method specific to the pair.

This vignette gives the definitions, the result for each window and the transform for each delay family. It then lists which pairs of window and delay the package solves analytically. The derivations are in the transform paper[1]. The double interval censored model is in Brand et al.[2].

2 Notation

The notation follows the transform paper[1].

Symbol Meaning In the package
\(F_{\mathrm{IP}}\), \(f_{\mathrm{IP}}\) CDF and density of the delay pdist and its arguments
\(w\), \(w_P\) width of the primary event window pwindow
\(z \in [0, w]\) primary event time, measured from the window start
\(q\) evaluation time, measured from the window start q of pcens_cdf()
\(f_{\mathrm{win}}(z; w)\) density of the primary event time in the window dprimary and primary_args
\(H_w(z)\) CDF of the primary event time in the window pprimary
\(F_{\mathrm{cens}}(q; w)\) primary event censored CDF pcens_cdf()
\(\rho\) exponential tilt of the window r of dexpgrowth()

The general results write the width as \(w\) and the window sections write it as \(w_P\). The window sections add the window parameters to \(f_{\mathrm{win}}\), for example \(f_{\mathrm{win}}(z; w_P, \rho)\). The subscript IP stands for incubation period. \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}\) may be any delay. A delay on the non-negative reals has \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}(x) = f_{\mathrm{IP}}(x) = 0\) for \(x < 0\). The main text of the transform paper takes the delay to be non-negative. The normal delay has support on the reals. For the normal delay the integrals over the delay \(u\) in equations (3.3), (3.4), (3.7) and (3.8) have lower limit \(-\infty\) instead of 0, as in the normal appendix of the transform paper. \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w)\) is then not zero for \(q < w\).

3 The transform reduction

The primary event censored CDF is

\[ F_{\mathrm{cens}}(q; w) = \int_0^w F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - z) f_{\mathrm{win}}(z; w)\,dz. \tag{3.1} \]

Let

\[ H_w(z) = \int_0^z f_{\mathrm{win}}(s; w)\,ds, \tag{3.2} \]

with \(H_w(z) = 0\) for \(z \leq 0\) and \(H_w(z) = 1\) for \(z \geq w\). Exchanging the order of integration in equation (3.1) gives

\[ F_{\mathrm{cens}}(q; w) = \int_0^q H_w(q - u) f_{\mathrm{IP}}(u)\,du. \tag{3.3} \]

The truncated exponential-moment transform of the delay density is

\[ T_f(\xi; \tau) = \int_0^\tau e^{\xi u} f_{\mathrm{IP}}(u)\,du, \tag{3.4} \]

with \(T_f(\xi; \tau) = 0\) for \(\tau \leq 0\) when the delay is non-negative. The delay CDF is \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}(\tau) = T_f(0; \tau)\). Suppose the reversed kernel \(H_w(q - u)\) has the expansion

\[ H_w(q - u) = \sum_k a_k(q, w) e^{\xi_k u} \tag{3.5} \]

for every \(u\) in the support of the delay up to \(q\). Substituting it into equation (3.3) gives

\[ F_{\mathrm{cens}}(q; w) = \sum_k a_k(q, w) T_f(\xi_k; q). \tag{3.6} \]

The window fixes the coefficients \(a_k(q, w)\) and the tilts \(\xi_k\). The delay fixes whether \(T_f\) is tractable at those tilts.

The reversed kernel is 1 for \(u \leq q - w\). This saturated part contributes \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w)\). The expansion is then needed only on \([q - w, q]\), and it may differ between parts of that interval. Each result below for the exponentially tilted, logistic and Gumbel windows has the form \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w)\) plus weighted differences \(T_f(\xi_k; \tau^+) - T_f(\xi_k; \tau^-)\). The endpoints \(\tau^\pm\) are \(q\) and \(q - w\), and for the logistic window also a split point \(u^\star\).

The uniform window uses the partial moment

\[ M(\tau) = \left. \frac{\partial T_f(\xi; \tau)}{\partial \xi} \right|_{\xi = 0} = \int_0^\tau u f_{\mathrm{IP}}(u)\,du \tag{3.7} \]

and, for \(n \geq 1\),

\[ K_n(t) = \int_0^t (t - u)^n f_{\mathrm{IP}}(u)\,du. \tag{3.8} \]

\(K_1(t)\) is the integral of \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}\) up to \(t\), and

\[ K_1(t) = t\,T_f(0; t) - M(t). \tag{3.9} \]

4 Primary event windows

Window R primary Stan primary id \(f_{\mathrm{win}}\) Tilts \(\xi_k\) Result
Uniform dunif 1 \(1 / w_P\) none, uses \(M\) (4.2)
Exponential tilt dexpgrowth(), r \(= \rho\) 2 \(\rho e^{\rho z} / (e^{\rho w_P} - 1)\) \(0\) and \(-\rho\) (4.1)
Truncated logistic dtlogis(), location \(= m\), scale \(= s\) 3 \(L'(z) / D_L\) \(n / s\) for \(n \geq 0\), \(-n / s\) for \(n \geq 1\) (4.3) to (4.5)
Truncated Gumbel dtgumbel(), mu \(= \mu_G\), beta \(= \beta\) 4 \(G'(z) / D_G\) \(n / \beta\) for \(n \geq 0\) (4.6)

4.1 Exponentially tilted window

The window density is \(f_{\mathrm{win}}(z; w_P, \rho) = \rho e^{\rho z} / (e^{\rho w_P} - 1)\) and the window CDF is

\[ H_{\rho, w_P}(z) = \frac{e^{\rho z} - 1}{e^{\rho w_P} - 1}, \qquad 0 \leq z \leq w_P. \]

A tilt \(\rho > 0\) places more mass late in the window, as for a growing primary event process[3,4]. A tilt \(\rho < 0\) places more mass early in the window. Let \(J_\rho(x) = T_f(-\rho; x)\). The CDF is

\[ F_\rho(q; w_P) = F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P) + \frac{e^{\rho q} \{J_\rho(q) - J_\rho(q - w_P)\} - \{F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q) - F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P)\}}{e^{\rho w_P} - 1}. \tag{4.1} \]

Collecting the \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P)\) terms gives the main result of the transform paper[1]. In the collected form the numerator loses precision through cancellation. Equation (4.1) keeps \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P)\) out of the numerator, and the package evaluates it on the log scale. Writing \(e^{\rho q} = e^{\rho w_P} e^{\rho (q - w_P)}\) makes each term a function of \(q\) or of \(q - w_P\) alone. For an integer pwindow of at least 1, \(q - w_P\) is an integer delay too. primarycensored_analytical_lcdf_vectorized() in Stan therefore computes the terms once per integer delay \(t\) and uses them for the CDF at \(t\) and at \(t + w_P\).

4.2 Uniform window as the limit \(\rho \to 0\)

As \(\rho \to 0\) the window density tends to \(1 / w_P\) and equation (4.1) tends to

\[ F_0(q; w_P) = F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P) + \frac{1}{w_P} \int_{q - w_P}^q (q - u) f_{\mathrm{IP}}(u)\,du = \frac{K_1(q) - K_1(q - w_P)}{w_P}. \tag{4.2} \]

By equation (3.9) this needs only \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}\) and the partial moment \(M\). It is closed form whenever \(M\) is. More families have a closed form \(M\) than a closed form tilted transform, for example the lognormal. Brand et al. give \(M\) for the gamma, lognormal and Weibull delays[2]. For a gamma delay with daily windows the resulting probability mass function matches that of Cori et al.[5].

4.3 Truncated logistic window

With midpoint \(m\) and scale \(s > 0\) let

\[ L(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(z - m) / s}}, \qquad D_L = L(w_P) - L(0), \qquad A(q) = e^{-(q - m) / s}, \qquad u^\star = q - m. \]

The window density is \(f_{\mathrm{win}}(z; w_P, m, s) = L'(z) / D_L\) and the window CDF is \(H_{L, w_P}(z) = \{L(z) - L(0)\} / D_L\). The reversed function \(L(q - u) = 1 / \{1 + A(q) e^{u / s}\}\) is a geometric series in \(e^{u / s}\) for \(u < u^\star\) and in \(e^{-u / s}\) for \(u > u^\star\). For \(m < 0\),

\[ F_L(q; w_P) = F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P) + \frac{1}{D_L} \Big[ \sum_{n = 0}^\infty (-1)^n A(q)^n \{T_f(n / s; q) - T_f(n / s; q - w_P)\} - L(0) \{F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q) - F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P)\} \Big]. \tag{4.3} \]

For \(m \geq w_P\),

\[ F_L(q; w_P) = F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P) + \frac{1}{D_L} \Big[ \sum_{n = 1}^\infty (-1)^{n - 1} A(q)^{-n} \{T_f(-n / s; q) - T_f(-n / s; q - w_P)\} - L(0) \{F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q) - F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P)\} \Big]. \tag{4.4} \]

For \(0 \leq m < w_P\) the integral is split at \(u^\star\),

\[ \begin{aligned} F_L(q; w_P) = F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P) + \frac{1}{D_L} \Big[ &\sum_{n = 0}^\infty (-1)^n A(q)^n \{T_f(n / s; u^\star) - T_f(n / s; q - w_P)\} \\ + &\sum_{n = 1}^\infty (-1)^{n - 1} A(q)^{-n} \{T_f(-n / s; q) - T_f(-n / s; u^\star)\} - L(0) \{F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q) - F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P)\} \Big]. \end{aligned} \tag{4.5} \]

4.4 Truncated Gumbel window

With location \(\mu_G\) and scale \(\beta > 0\) let

\[ G(z) = \exp\left[-e^{-(z - \mu_G) / \beta}\right], \qquad D_G = G(w_P) - G(0), \qquad c(q) = e^{-(q - \mu_G) / \beta}. \]

The window density is \(f_{\mathrm{win}}(z; w_P, \mu_G, \beta) = G'(z) / D_G\) and the window CDF is \(H_{G, w_P}(z) = \{G(z) - G(0)\} / D_G\). The reversed function \(G(q - u) = \exp\{-c(q) e^{u / \beta}\}\) is a power series in \(e^{u / \beta}\), which gives

\[ F_G(q; w_P) = F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P) + \frac{1}{D_G} \Big[ \sum_{n = 0}^\infty \frac{\{-c(q)\}^n}{n!} \{T_f(n / \beta; q) - T_f(n / \beta; q - w_P)\} - G(0) \{F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q) - F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q - w_P)\} \Big]. \tag{4.6} \]

The series converges for every \(q\) and needs no split.

5 Delay transforms

The table gives \(T_f\) and \(M\) for each delay family with a transform in the package. \(\gamma(\alpha, x)\) is the lower incomplete gamma function and \(P(\alpha, x) = \gamma(\alpha, x) / \Gamma(\alpha)\). \(\Phi\) and \(\phi\) are the standard normal CDF and density. The classes are those of the transform paper[1]. A transform is analytic if it is a closed form in elementary or standard functions such as \(P\) and \(\Phi\), semi-analytic if it needs a convergent series of special functions, and numerical if it needs quadrature. The numerical class is distinct from the numerical method, which integrates equation (3.1) directly.

Family (R; Stan id) \(T_f(\xi; \tau)\) \(M(\tau)\) Class Transform used when
Exponential, rate \(\lambda\) (pexp; 4) \(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda - \xi} \{1 - e^{-(\lambda - \xi) \tau}\}\) \(P(2, \lambda \tau) / \lambda\) analytic \(\xi < \lambda\)
Gamma, shape \(\alpha\), rate \(\lambda\) (pgamma; 2) \(\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda - \xi}\right)^\alpha P(\alpha, (\lambda - \xi) \tau)\) \(\frac{\alpha}{\lambda} P(\alpha + 1, \lambda \tau)\) analytic \(\xi < \lambda\)
Normal, mean \(\mu\), standard deviation \(\sigma\) (pnorm; 18) \(e^{\xi \mu + \xi^2 \sigma^2 / 2}\, \Phi\left(\frac{\tau - \mu - \xi \sigma^2}{\sigma}\right)\) \(\mu \Phi(z_\tau) - \sigma \phi(z_\tau)\), \(z_\tau = \frac{\tau - \mu}{\sigma}\) analytic always
Weibull, shape \(k\), scale \(\lambda\) (pweibull; 3) \(\sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{(\xi \lambda)^n}{n!} \gamma\left(1 + \frac{n}{k}, (\tau / \lambda)^k\right)\) \(\lambda \gamma\left(1 + \frac{1}{k}, (\tau / \lambda)^k\right)\) semi-analytic \(|\xi| \tau < 400\) and the checks under Numerical safeguards pass
Generalised gamma, \((a, b, c)\) (pgengamma.orig; 5, and pgengamma in R) \(\sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{\xi^n}{n!} b^{-n / c} \frac{\gamma(a + n / c, b \tau^c)}{\Gamma(a)}\) \(b^{-1 / c} \frac{\gamma(a + 1 / c, b \tau^c)}{\Gamma(a)}\) semi-analytic \(|\xi| \tau < 400\) and the checks under Numerical safeguards pass
Lognormal, \(\mu\), \(\sigma\) (plnorm; 1) \(\int_{-\infty}^{\log \tau} e^{\xi e^x} \frac{1}{\sigma} \phi\left(\frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}\right) dx\) \(e^{\mu + \sigma^2 / 2}\, \Phi\left(\frac{\log \tau - \mu}{\sigma} - \sigma\right)\) numerical for \(\xi < 0\), semi-analytic for \(\xi > 0\) \(\xi < 0\) with \(\log(-\xi) + 2 \log \sigma + \mu < 690\), or \(\xi > 0\) within the series limits below

The generalised gamma row uses the density \(c b^a u^{a c - 1} e^{-b u^c} / \Gamma(a)\) of the transform paper. The Stacy form of flexsurv::pgengamma.orig()[6] has shape \(= c\), scale \(= b^{-1 / c}\) and k \(= a\). The Weibull is the case \(a = 1\). The Prentice form of flexsurv::pgengamma() with \(Q > 0\) is mapped in R to the Stacy form with shape \(= Q / \sigma\), scale \(= e^\mu Q^{2 \sigma / Q}\) and k \(= Q^{-2}\). For \(Q \leq 0\) the numerical method is used.

The lognormal transform has no closed form. The package uses Gauss-Legendre quadrature for \(\xi < 0\). For \(\xi > 0\) it uses the series \(\sum_{j \geq 0} \xi^j e^{j \mu + j^2 \sigma^2 / 2} \Phi\left(\frac{\log \tau - \mu}{\sigma} - j \sigma\right) / j!\) of positive terms. In R this series is used where \(\xi \tau \leq 200\) or \(\xi w_P > 2\). In Stan it is used where \(\xi \tau \leq 60\) or \(\xi w_P > 2\). Both use at most 20000 terms. Elsewhere the numerical method is used for that \(q\).

Some families have a closed form \(M\) or \(K_1\) but no tilted transform in the package. They have analytic solutions for the uniform window only. Here \(I_x(\cdot, \cdot)\) is the regularised incomplete beta function, \(A_\tau = (\tau / \lambda)^k\) and \(r_a\) is defined below.

Family (Stan id) \(M(\tau)\) or \(K_1(t)\) Needs Available in
Log-logistic, shape \(k\), scale \(\lambda\) (29) \(M(\tau) = \tau F_{\mathrm{IP}}(\tau) r_{1 / k}(A_\tau)\) \(k \geq 0.01\) R and Stan
Beta, shapes \(\alpha_1\), \(\alpha_2\) (9) \(M(\tau) = \frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha_1 + \alpha_2} I_{\min(\tau, 1)}(\alpha_1 + 1, \alpha_2)\) non-centrality 0 R and Stan
Chi-square, \(\nu\) degrees of freedom (13) the gamma with \(\alpha = \nu / 2\) and \(\lambda = 1 / 2\) non-centrality 0 R and Stan
Inverse gamma, shape \(\alpha\), scale \(\theta\) (16) \(M(\tau) = \frac{\theta}{\alpha - 1} \{1 - P(\alpha - 1, \theta / \tau)\}\) \(\alpha > 1\) Stan
Inverse chi-square, \(\nu\) (19) the inverse gamma with \(\alpha = \nu / 2\) and \(\theta = 1 / 2\) \(\nu > 2\) Stan
Scaled inverse chi-square, \(\nu\) and scale \(\varsigma\) (22) the inverse gamma with \(\alpha = \nu / 2\) and \(\theta = \nu \varsigma^2 / 2\) \(\nu > 2\) Stan
Pareto, shape \(\alpha\), minimum \(y_m\) (21) \(K_1(t) = y_m \left\{e^{\ell} - 1 + \frac{e^{-(\alpha - 1) \ell} - 1}{\alpha - 1}\right\}\), \(\ell = \log(t / y_m)\), for \(t \geq y_m\) Stan

For the Pareto with \(\alpha = 1\) the second term takes its limit \(-\ell\). The non-central beta and chi-square use the numerical method.

The log-logistic ratio is

\[ r_a(A_\tau) = \frac{1 + A_\tau}{A_\tau^{a + 1}} \int_0^{A_\tau} \frac{y^a}{(1 + y)^2}\,dy. \]

For a delay \(U\) with CDF \(F_{\mathrm{IP}}\) it is \(E[(U / \tau)^{a k} \mid U \leq \tau]\). The integral is a Gauss hypergeometric function, which base R does not have, so the package evaluates \(r_a\) by one of three series in \(A_\tau\). In Stan the log-logistic parameters are ordered [scale, shape].

The step and hazard delays of pdiscretestep() and pdiscretehazard() (Stan ids 26, 27 and 28) do not use a transform. Their CDF is piecewise constant, so equation (3.1) is a finite sum of differences of the window CDF. In R pcens_cdf.pcens_pdiscretestep() and pcens_cdf.pcens_pdiscretehazard() compute this exactly for any window with a pprimary function.

6 Coverage by window and delay

The table lists the pairs of window and delay that the package solves. Each entry is the class of the quantities the window needs, “exact” for a finite sum, or “numerical method”. The uniform window needs \(M\) or \(K_1\), and the other windows need \(T_f\). The log-logistic \(M\) is semi-analytic because it is evaluated by series in \(A_\tau\). The logistic and Gumbel windows add a truncated series over the tilts. The R method for a pair is pcens_cdf.pcens_p<delay>_d<primary>, for example pcens_cdf.pcens_pgamma_dexpgrowth().

Delay Uniform Exponential tilt Truncated logistic Truncated Gumbel
Exponential analytic analytic if \(\lambda > -\rho\) analytic if \(m \geq w_P\) or \(\lambda\) exceeds the largest tilt numerical method
Gamma analytic analytic if \(\lambda > -\rho\) analytic if \(m \geq w_P\) or \(\lambda\) exceeds the largest tilt numerical method
Normal analytic analytic analytic analytic
Weibull analytic semi-analytic numerical method numerical method
Generalised gamma analytic semi-analytic numerical method numerical method
Lognormal analytic numerical for \(\rho > 0\), semi-analytic for \(\rho < 0\) numerical method numerical method
Log-logistic semi-analytic numerical method numerical method numerical method
Beta, chi-square analytic numerical method numerical method numerical method
Inverse gamma, inverse chi-square, scaled inverse chi-square, Pareto analytic in Stan, numerical method in R numerical method numerical method numerical method
Step and hazard exact exact exact exact in R, numerical method in Stan

The logistic window needs the tilts \(n / s\) and \(-n / s\) up to the number of series terms. For \(m \geq w_P\) it needs no positive tilt. The Gumbel window needs the tilts \(n / \beta\) for \(n = 0, \ldots, N\), with \(N\) at least 2. The normal delay has a transform at every tilt, and is the only delay the package pairs with the Gumbel window. The Gumbel series checks under Numerical safeguards still apply to it. The Weibull, generalised gamma and lognormal delays have transforms, but no method pairs them with the logistic or Gumbel windows.

In Stan primarycensored_cdf() and primarycensored_lcdf() choose between the analytical and the numerical path with check_for_analytical_params(). It takes pwindow, as the admissibility of some windows, such as the truncated logistic, depends on it. primarycensored_analytical_lcdf() rejects parameters that fail these checks.

Window Stan functions Parameter check
Uniform primarycensored_<dist>_uniform_terms() and primarycensored_uniform_lcdf_from_terms() check_for_uniform_terms() and check_uniform_terms_params()

Truncated logistic primarycensored_tlogis_lcdf() and primarycensored_tlogis_lcdf_vectorized() check_for_tlogis_params()

For the Gumbel window, with any delay, and for the log-logistic delay with the uniform window the numerical method is specific to the pair. In R these are .gumbel_numeric() and .loglogistic_numeric_cdf(). In Stan they are primarycensored_gumbel_numeric_lcdf() and loglogistic_numeric_lcdf(). 7 Numerical safeguards

7.1 Small tilt

The numerator of equation (4.1) loses precision through cancellation as \(\rho \to 0\). For a gamma delay the loss grows with the shape. For \(|\rho| w_P < 10^{-2}\), or \(10^{-3}\) for delays on the reals, and \(|\rho| (|q| + w_P) < 0.1\), the package replaces equation (4.1) with its Taylor expansion in \(\rho\) about the uniform solution, written in the \(K_n\) of equation (3.8). To first order this is \(F_0(q; w_P) + \rho \{K_2(q) - w_P K_1(q) - K_2(q - w_P) - w_P K_1(q - w_P)\} / (2 w_P)\). The package also keeps the second order term, \(\rho^2 [2 \{K_3(q) - K_3(q - w_P)\} - 3 w_P \{K_2(q) + K_2(q - w_P)\} + w_P^2 \{K_1(q) - K_1(q - w_P)\}] / (12 w_P)\), so the error is third order, \(O\big((\rho w_P)^3\big)\). The relative truncation error is below \((|\rho| w_P)^3 / 160\).

This form subtracts terms of the size of \(|q| + w_P\), so its rounding error grows with the distance from the origin. Equation (4.1) has a rounding error of about \(10^{-15} / (|\rho| w_P)\) at any \(q\). The expansion has the smaller error while \(|\rho| (|q| + w_P)\) is below about 0.1, so equation (4.1) is used beyond that. In R .exptilt_cdf_finite() and in Stan primarycensored_exptilt_form() choose the form for each delay.

7.2 Small delay

For a delay on the non-negative reals with \(q < w_P\) the exponential tilt CDF is \(\{e^{\rho q} J_\rho(q) - F_{\mathrm{IP}}(q)\} / (e^{\rho w_P} - 1)\). For \(|\rho| q < 5 \times 10^{-3}\) the package replaces the numerator with its Taylor expansion in \(\rho\), \(\rho K_1(q) + \rho^2 K_2(q) / 2 + \rho^3 K_3(q) / 6\). The relative truncation error is below \((|\rho| q)^3 / 24\). The errors of both small tilt forms are below \(10^{-8}\) at these limits. For delays on the non-negative reals the \(K_n\) are computed from the partial moments \(\int_0^t u^j f_{\mathrm{IP}}(u)\,du\), \(j = 0, \ldots, 3\), by .moments_from_partial() in R and primarycensored_moments_from_partial() in Stan. The logistic window uses \(\{L'(0) K_1(q) + L''(0) K_2(q) / 2\} / D_L\) for \(q < w_P\) and \(q < 10^{-4} s\).

7.3 Tail choice

A transform difference is taken from the lower transforms or from the upper transforms \(T_f(\xi; \infty) - T_f(\xi; \tau)\), whichever loses less precision. The exponential, gamma and normal have upper transforms for every admissible tilt, the lognormal for \(\xi \leq 0\) and the other families only at \(\xi = 0\).

7.4 Weibull and generalised gamma series

The series is used only where \(|\xi| \tau < 400\) and it converges within 400 terms. For \(\xi < 0\) its terms alternate, and it is used only where the sum of the absolute terms is below \(10^5\) times the transform. R and Stan apply this check in the same way.

These series have no upper tail form, so a second check is made at each \(q\) on the numerator of equation (4.1). It compares the size of the terms of the numerator, divided by \(e^{\rho w_P} - 1\), with a reference. Where the ratio is above \(10^5\) that \(q\) uses the numerical method. In R the reference is the smaller of the CDF and its survival function, so the check bounds the relative error in both tails. In Stan the reference is 1, so the check bounds the absolute error of the CDF at about \(10^{-11}\). Upper tail probability masses of about this size or smaller can therefore lose relative accuracy in Stan.

7.5 Log-logistic partial moment

The uniform solution differences \(K_1(t) = t F_{\mathrm{IP}}(t) \{1 - r_{1 / k}(A_t)\}\) at \(q\) and \(q - w_P\). Each \(q\) is screened with a bound on the rounding error of this difference. That \(q\) uses the numerical method where the bound exceeds \(10^{-8}\) times the smaller of the CDF and its survival function, or \(10^{-6}\) times the density of \(F_{\mathrm{cens}}\). R and Stan use the same rule.

7.6 Logistic series

The geometric series converge slowly near \(u^\star\). They are summed with a binomial taper of the partial sums (Euler summation) to an error below \(10^{-10} D_L\), with at most 64 terms.

7.7 Gumbel series

The terms alternate. The sum of their absolute values is up to about \(e^{c(0)}\) times the delay mass in the window, so the relative precision lost grows as \(e^{c(0)}\). The series is used only for \(c(0) \leq 15\) and where its estimated relative error is below \(10^{-8}\). The estimate adds the rounding error, from the sum of the absolute terms, and a bound on the truncation error. Where it is above \(10^{-8}\) that \(q\) uses the numerical method.

8 Departures from the paper

  1. The exponential and gamma transforms are finite for every \(\xi\), but the package has no stable form for \(\xi \geq \lambda\).
  2. The lognormal transform is semi-analytic for \(\xi > 0\), where the transform paper evaluates it by quadrature.
  3. The transform paper states the logistic regimes with strict inequalities. The package includes the boundaries as above.
  4. The logistic and Gumbel series coefficients are rearranged so that the \(L(0)\) and \(G(0)\) terms do not cancel when \(D_L\) or \(D_G\) is small. The result is unchanged.

9 Extending the package

A new delay needs its transform. In R it needs methods for .pcens_tilt_transform(), .pcens_tilt_available(), .pcens_tilt_lower() and .pcens_tilt_moments(). In Stan it needs an entry in log_tilt_transform_pair(), primarycensored_tilt_moments(), check_for_tilt_transform() and check_for_exptilt(). A delay whose transform holds only at some q also needs the per-point checks that the lognormal uses, .pcens_tilt_fits() in R and check_for_tilt_transform_at() in Stan. A pair of window and delay then needs its pcens_cdf method in R and its dispatch in Stan.
